title: Fed’s Barr: Surge of Investment and Related Demand from AI Buildout is Having Measurable Effect on Prices
key_facts: Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr said on Tuesday (29 Sep 2026), in a speech in Detroit, that higher energy prices and AI together have knocked the Fed off course toward its 2% inflation goal.
Barr said the surge of investment and demand from the AI build-out is having a "measurable effect" on prices.
He said he counts only two months of data consistent with 2% core PCE inflation over the past 20 months and does not yet see a clear trend toward a timely return to 2%.
Barr said he expects further interest rate rises to be needed because inflation risks have increased.
He said the effects from tariffs have diminished, but energy prices are still high and it is uncertain when the Iran war's effect on prices will be resolved.
New York Fed president John Williams said the inflationary effect of the AI-related demand shock is "increasingly salient".

The Fed raised rates a few weeks ago for the first time in more than three years; the median expectation, excluding Chairman Kevin Warsh, is one more rise this year, and the market has priced in three.
quote_evidence: At the same time, he noted the surge of investment and demand from the AI build-out is having a "measurable effect" on prices.
Barr said he expects further interest rate hikes to be needed to bring down inflation, as inflation risks have increased.

why_it_matters_hint: A Federal Reserve governor says AI-related spending is helping to keep prices up, and expects more interest rate rises.
